common_name: Luscious Lantana (Sterile Non-Seeding Landscape Lantana Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Luscious was bred to be sterile or nearly so, producing very few seeds and reducing the self-seeding and bird-spread naturalization that has made some older lantana cultivars invasive in mild climates.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, and water sparingly once established, since lantana is highly drought-tolerant and prone to root and crown rot in consistently wet soil. Luscious is a vegetatively propagated lantana series bred for a low, spreading, well-branched habit and a bright range of citrus and berry-toned flower colors, produced in continuous flushes from spring through frost that draw butterflies and hummingbirds heavily. Its low seed set is a meaningful improvement over older, heavily self-seeding lantana cultivars that have become weedy or invasive in warm, frost-free climates, making Luscious a more responsible choice for gardeners in the Deep South and similar regions. In milder winters the roots often survive to resprout in spring; where hard freezes occur it is grown as a warm-season annual.
sources: Proven Winners — Luscious lantana series notes
University of Florida IFAS Extension — invasive lantana cultivar research

common_name: Rockin' Salvia (Vigorous Heat-Tolerant Hummingbird Sage Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to moderately moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Rockin' salvia grows larger and more vigorously than the species type, so give it room to spread into a substantial clump over the season.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moderately moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and give this vigorous selection plenty of room to grow into a large, well-branched clump by late summer. Rockin' is a bred selection of Salvia guaranitica (anise sage) valued for larger flowers, more vigorous growth, and better heat tolerance than the species or older cultivars like Black and Blue, producing spikes of large, deep blue to purple tubular flowers continuously from summer through frost that are outstanding for hummingbirds. Its exceptional vigor and heat tolerance make it a standout performer through the peak of Gulf South summer, when many perennials slow their bloom, and the substantial size makes it a strong anchor plant for the back of a mixed border. Where winters are mild the rhizomatous roots often survive to resprout in spring; further north it can be treated as an annual or mulched heavily for winter protection.
sources: Proven Winners — Rockin' salvia series notes

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic potting mix in full sun after the last frost; Superbells is a vegetatively propagated, sterile hybrid series that does not come true from seed and is sold exclusively as rooted cuttings or potted plants.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic potting mix in full sun after the last frost, and feed regularly with a balanced or slightly acidic fertilizer, since calibrachoa is a heavy feeder that performs poorly in alkaline soil or without consistent nutrition. Superbells is a leading vegetatively propagated calibrachoa (million bells) series bred for improved vigor, disease resistance, and an especially wide range of flower colors and patterns, from solids to stars, veins, and picotee edges, on trailing stems that spill attractively from hanging baskets, window boxes, and containers. The small, petunia-like flowers are produced in overwhelming numbers continuously from spring through frost without deadheading, making it one of the most popular container annuals for Gulf South porches and patios. Pinch back stems if trailing growth becomes leggy by midsummer to encourage fresh, dense rebloom.
sources: Proven Winners — Superbells calibrachoa series notes
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Trial Garden Reports

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens after the last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile potting mix in full sun; Whirlwind is a vegetatively propagated selection bred for improved vigor and heat tolerance over older scaevola cultivars, performing especially well through Gulf South summer humidity.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile potting mix in full sun after the last frost, and water consistently, since scaevola performs best without letting the root zone dry out completely between waterings. Whirlwind is a heat-tolerant, vigorously trailing fan flower selection producing an abundance of distinctive, one-sided, fan-shaped flowers in blue, purple, or white continuously from spring through frost, spilling attractively over the edges of hanging baskets, window boxes, and raised containers. Bred for stronger heat and humidity tolerance than older scaevola cultivars, it holds up notably well through the peak of Gulf South summer, when many trailing annuals decline, and requires no deadheading to keep blooming. Its long, trailing stems benefit from an occasional light trim if growth becomes overly leggy, encouraging fuller, more floriferous regrowth.
sources: Proven Winners — Whirlwind scaevola series notes

common_name: Blue My Mind Evolvulus (True-Blue Trailing Dwarf Morning Glory)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings after the last frost in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; excellent drainage is essential, as with all evolvulus, and Blue My Mind was bred for a more vigorous, floriferous habit than older blue daze selections. In zone 9–11 it behaves as a perennial.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, sandy soil in full sun, and take care not to overwater, since evolvulus rots quickly in heavy, moisture-retentive soil. Blue My Mind is a vigorous, heavy-flowering selection of dwarf morning glory prized for its unusually true, vivid sky-blue flowers, a color rare among heat-tolerant summer annuals, produced in enormous numbers over small, silvery-green, fuzzy foliage on low, trailing stems from spring through frost. It performs best in hot, dry conditions and is an excellent choice for containers, hanging baskets, rock gardens, and the front of a sunny border where its intense blue color can be appreciated up close. In zones 9–11 it persists as a woody-based perennial in a protected, well-drained site; elsewhere it is grown as a warm-season annual, propagated by cuttings taken before frost.
sources: Proven Winners — Blue My Mind evolvulus variety notes
